objective.en: Write a story with a character, setting, problem, events, dialogue and ending, in your own sentences.
objective.es: Escribir un cuento con personaje, lugar, problema, sucesos, diálogo y final, con tus propias oraciones.

success.en: I can tell who the story is about and where it happens.
success.es: Puedo decir de quién trata el cuento y dónde ocurre.

success.en: I can write what goes wrong and what happens next, in order.
success.es: Puedo escribir qué sale mal y qué pasa después, en orden.

success.en: I can write what a character says with quotation marks.
success.es: Puedo escribir lo que dice un personaje con comillas.

success.en: I can make my story clearer when I read it again.
success.es: Puedo aclarar mi cuento cuando lo vuelvo a leer.

narrative: Tala the Storyteller has an empty stage and a trunk full of story pieces. Choose a character, a place and a problem. Then write the story yourself, one part at a time, and watch the stage act out your words.

scene.alt: A small theater stage with red curtains and a wooden floor. A trunk full of story pieces sits to one side. Tala the Storyteller stands at the edge of the stage holding a book.

vocab.def: A person or animal in a story.
Where and when the story happens.
What goes wrong in the story.
The exact words that characters say.
How the problem is solved at the end.

items.prompt: Read Tala's short model story. Open every part and notice what each part does.

sources.title: Who and where
text: Rosa the owl lived in a tall pine tree at the edge of a quiet forest.

sources.title: The problem
text: One windy night, her lantern fell and its light went out.

sources.title: Events
text: First, Rosa looked on the ground, but it was too dark. Then she asked the fireflies for help.

sources.title: Dialogue
text: "Please light my lantern," said Rosa. "I cannot find my way home."

sources.title: Resolution
text: In the end, the fireflies lit the lantern, and Rosa flew home safely.

items.prompt: Sort each sentence from a new story. Which part of a story is it?

cards.text: Kofi the fox lived in a cozy den by the river.
cards.why: This tells you who and where. Look for a name and a place.

cards.text: One morning, the bridge over the river was gone!
cards.why: Something goes wrong here. What changed?

cards.text: First, Kofi tried to jump across, but the water was too wide.
cards.why: A character tries something. Look for 'first' or 'then'.

cards.text: Then he asked the beaver to help him build a new bridge.
cards.why: This is the next thing that happens. Look for 'then'.

cards.text: At last, the new bridge was ready, and Kofi walked across happily.
cards.why: The problem is solved here. Look for 'at last' or 'in the end'.

cards.text: A little rabbit named Lulu lived on a hill near the sea.
cards.why: This tells you who and where.

items.prompt: Pick your character, place and problem. Then write one sentence for each part in your own words. After each sentence, the stage acts it out.

slots.label: Who and where
slots.hint: Tell who the story is about and where they are.

checks.label: Names your character and your place
checks.hint: Use the names you picked, or a word that means the same.

slots.label: First event
slots.hint: What does your character try first?

checks.label: Uses a time word like first

slots.label: Next event
slots.hint: What happens next? Show a different try.

checks.label: Uses a time word like then or next

slots.label: Dialogue
slots.hint: What does your character say? Put the exact words in quotation marks.

checks.label: Uses quotation marks around the spoken words

items.prompt: Read your whole story. Change at least three words to make it clearer or more exciting. You could add a describing word, a feeling or a sound.
items.purpose: Tala will read your best version.

checks.label: Still has the character's spoken words in quotation marks
Still shows the order with time words

ladder.model: Model: change 'the dark night' to 'the cold, dark night'. Change 'said Rosa' to 'whispered Rosa'.
ladder.frame: I added the describing word ___ before ___. I changed ___ to ___.
ladder.cue: Find one plain word. Swap it for a stronger word.

items.prompt: Tell your story to a partner in your own words. Use the words first, then, and in the end.

ladder.frame: My story is about ___. The problem is ___. First, ___. Then, ___. In the end, ___.
ladder.partial: My story is about ___. First, ___. In the end, ___.

selfChecks.label: I told the parts in order.
I used first, then or in the end.
I used a clear, steady voice.

endings.title: The curtain rises
endings.text: Tala claps. 'You wrote the parts in order, and you made your own changes to improve it. Every word on that stage is yours.'

endings.title: A story on the stage
endings.text: Tala smiles as the curtain rises. 'You built every part of your story. Next time, try changing a few words to make it even clearer.'

skill.en: writing a story with a beginning, a problem, events in order, dialogue and an ending
skill.es: escribir un cuento con inicio, problema, sucesos en orden, diálogo y final

talk.en: Ask: 'Who is your story about? What problem did your character have? How did it end?'
talk.es: Pregunta: '¿De quién trata tu cuento? ¿Qué problema tuvo tu personaje? ¿Cómo terminó?'
